description: We are CodeX, a team of students and developers passionate about AI, Big Data, software development, and real-world problem solving. We enjoy learning, sharing ideas, and building useful solutions together. We are looking for teammates interested in AI, data science, ML, design, research, or other skills who are motivated to learn, collaborate, and build something meaningful.
summary: We built AgriBot, a voice assistant on WhatsApp that turns 25 years of NASA climate data into crop rotation advice for smallholder farmers in northern and central Côte d'Ivoire. In Korhogo and Bouaké, the start of the rainy season moves by weeks from year to year, and many farmers cannot read written advice. The farmer simply sends a voice note. Our engine computes each crop's daily water need with the FAO-56 method from NASA POWER data (MERRA-2 and CERES), compares it with GPM IMERG rainfall from 2001 to 2025, and ranks three rotations, including the farmer's current one, with uncertainty ranges. AgriBot answers in one or two plain sentences, by voice. It also compares recent NASA HLS satellite images with past years to flag weak vegetation, gives a cautious first opinion on photos of sick plants, and never names a pesticide. An offline web app serves areas without a network. This matters because better rotation choices protect harvests and incomes as rains shift. AgriBot is honest about uncertainty: it announces a climate shift only when two independent NASA sources agree, and it always refers farmers to their ANADER advisor.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

AgriBot helps smallholder farmers in the Poro (Korhogo) and Gbêkê (Bouaké) regions of Côte d'Ivoire choose crop rotations that fit the climate of their area. It reaches them through two channels: a voice assistant on WhatsApp, and an offline web app for areas without a network.

1. NASA data. We use daily GPM IMERG rainfall (mean of the 9 cells around each town), MERRA-2 temperature, dew point, wind and corrected rainfall, and CERES solar radiation, all through the NASA POWER API from 2001 to 2025. Through NASA AppEEARS we use MODIS MCD12Q1 land cover to select 50 vegetation points per town, and Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) NDVI with its cloud mask from 2013 to November 2026.

2. Engine. FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration, multiplied by each crop's coefficient, gives the daily water need. Rain onset is the first 20 mm in 3 days after 1 March with no dry spell over 7 days in the next 30. For every year we check whether rain covers each crop's need over its cycle and whether a dry spell hits the sensitive mid-season stage. Three rotations are scored on water, market access and soil nitrogen: cotton then maize (current practice), cotton-cowpea-maize, and sorghum then cowpea. The farmer's priority weighs 0.6. Every score has a 90% bootstrap interval, and the ranking is tested against 20% less rain, a 14-day later onset, and other cotton sowing dates and cycle lengths.

3. Vegetation alert. For each image date, the zone NDVI is the median of cloud-free HLS observations. If it falls below the 10th percentile of the same calendar window in past years, AgriBot warns that vegetation is weaker than usual, without ever guessing a cause.

4. WhatsApp delivery. A FastAPI webhook verifies Meta's signature and drives a dialogue state machine. Voice notes are transcribed by Whisper on Groq, with a local faster-whisper model as fallback. Short answers to free farming questions come from gpt-oss-120b on Groq under a strict JSON schema. Replies are read aloud by Aethex streaming text-to-speech. Google Gemini gives a first opinion on plant photos.

5. Offline web app. All recommendations are precomputed. The installable app runs with no server and no network once loaded. It shows pictograms on every button and reads every message aloud. A MobileNetV3 maize leaf model, trained by our team, runs inside the browser.

RESULTS

For water, sorghum then cowpea scores 4.65 out of 5 in Korhogo and 4.35 in Bouaké, against 4.05 and 2.97 for today's cotton then maize. Bouaké is more exposed to water shortage. At Korhogo, rain onset ranged from 24 March (2013) to 28 May (2017). Between 2001-2012 and 2013-2025, IMERG finds a 22-day later onset at Korhogo but MERRA-2 a 22-day earlier one, so AgriBot announces no change. On 2 November 2026, vegetation around Korhogo was within its usual range; Bouaké was too cloudy for a reliable comparison, and AgriBot says so.

BENEFITS

- Farmers who cannot read get climate-informed advice by voice, on the phone they already own.

- Advice is local, sourced and honest about uncertainty, and it names the scenario that would change it.

- It works with or without network.

- It supports the ANADER extension service rather than replacing it.

EXPECTED IMPACT

Better rotation choices protect harvests and incomes as the start of the rains shifts. The vegetation alert flags problems early. Extension advisors gain a tool that explains every number. The approach scales to any town covered by NASA POWER and HLS.

TOOLS

- Languages and libraries: Python 3.12, pandas, NumPy, Pydantic, FastAPI, Uvicorn, SQLite, Streamlit, Jupyter (one notebook per CRISP-DM phase), PyAV for audio.

- Messaging and AI services: WhatsApp Cloud API, Groq (gpt-oss-120b, whisper-large-v3-turbo), faster-whisper, Aethex text-to-speech, Google Gemini.

- Offline app: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, a service worker, ONNX Runtime Web, the Web Speech API, and Google Colab for training the leaf model.

- Development: Claude Code (Anthropic) as an AI coding assistant.

- Quality: 265 automated tests for the main project and 20 for the offline app.

- Hardware: laptops and Android phones.

CREATIVITY

Satellite and reanalysis data reach farmers as a voice note, with nothing to install and nothing to read. The AI only listens, speaks and looks at photos; every recommendation comes from a transparent, sourced engine. A climate shift is told to farmers only when two independent NASA sources agree.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Literacy: voice first, pictograms, plain words.

- Connectivity: an offline app and a light WhatsApp channel.

- Consent: asked in the first message, and "stop" erases everything.

- Privacy: phone numbers stored only as a salted hash; photos and voice notes never saved by AgriBot.

- Safety: no pesticide or product ever named, never speaking on behalf of ANADER.

- Scientific honesty: uncertainty ranges, sensitivity tests, a two-source rule, and stated limits.

- Data limits: 500 m MODIS pixels miss small fields, and cloud cover reduces what HLS can see.

- Cost: AI calls kept low and voice credits capped each day.
